subject: Multi-zone attack tree and tenancy assurance — evidence and next steps

Cc: security@northbridge.com

Subject: Request: multi-zone attack tree + isolation evidence for procurement review

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — as part of our procurement security review we need a concise attack-tree oriented summary that shows how Redwood prevents cross-tenant impact across multizone deployments. Our reviewers want: 1) an attack-tree (PDF) mapping high-level attacker goals to mitigations, 2) a network diagram showing zone boundaries and egress controls, and 3) evidence artifacts (logs/config snippets) demonstrating isolation controls.

Can you provide these items, plus a short explanatory memo we can hand to our auditors? Ideally by end of next week. Also, a quick call to walk through the diagram would be helpful.

Thanks,
Stefan Leroy
Head of Infrastructure Security
NorthBridge Financial

--
Note: please send any large files as drive links or tarballs.

Hi Stefan — thanks for the clear ask. We're preparing a focused packet. At a high level: Redwood's multi-zone model uses strict control-plane/data-plane demarcation, per-tenant routing enclaves, and egress policy enforcement at the zone edge. Our packet will include an attack-tree PDF, the annotated network diagram, and a tarball with evidence excerpts (config, sample audit logs, and KV cache isolation test results).

Attachments (to follow): multizone-attack-tree.pdf; redwood-zone-network-diagram.vsdx; tenancy-segregation-evidence.tar.gz

Vanessa — can you attach the diagram and the attack-tree export? Marissa — I'll include the audit-snippet package and a one-page memo for the auditors.

We can also do a 30-min walkthrough; propose Thu Jun 10 10:00-10:30 PT or Fri Jun 11 09:00-09:30 PT. Which works for you?

Regards,
Irene Choi

Stefan / Irene — attaching the requested artifacts. Short notes below; see attachments and the Drive link for the editable Visio and detailed notes.

1) multizone-attack-tree.pdf (attachment) — top-level attacker objectives mapped to mitigation controls. Key nodes called out: control-plane compromise, tenant-credential-exfiltration, KV-cache poisoning, lateral egress via sidecars. For each node we list detection counters, expected telemetry, and fallback policies (e.g., model fallback to lower-capacity zone).

2) redwood-zone-network-diagram.vsdx (Drive link + attachment) — shows three layered zones: control plane (private, no tenant data), compute/tenant zones (per-tenant virtual enclaves with enforced routing), and egress/ingress DMZ with egress proxies and per-tenant NAT policies. Diagram includes sample NSG rules and port lists for common services.

3) tenancy-segregation-evidence.tar.gz (attachment) — contains: sample VPC flow logs showing denied lateral attempts, control-plane audit excerpt (HSM/KMS access history), and a small test harness log demonstrating KV cache namespace enforcement. We redact PII and customer identifiers.

Operational notes:
- Isolation enforced by per-tenant ACLs in the dataplane layer plus prefix-level KV namespaces.
- The runtime uses strict memory partitioning and per-worker tenant IDs to reduce cross-tenant leakage risk.
- We include automated regression checks in CI that run isolation unit tests on our deployment images.

Call: Thu Jun 10 10:00 PT works for me — I'll add calendar invite once Stefan confirms.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Solutions Architect, Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: multizone-attack-tree.pdf (9 pages), redwood-zone-network-diagram.vsdx (1 file), tenancy-segregation-evidence.tar.gz (1 archive, ~3.4MB)
